author: Claude
method: finite table lookups over the fixed engine (legacy_research/work/superperm_partial_f1.py) plus the supplied 1818-anchor corpus

q1_why_OTHER.answer: it is the UNIQUE anchor in the corpus whose hub-completer is a Z3
q1_why_OTHER.note: OTHER is a correct descriptive name for the one anchor outside the {R,Z2} completer dichotomy, not a fallback bucket
q1_why_OTHER.second_uniqueness: also the only anchor (1 of 1818) whose canonical hub_id equals the engine literal HUB=0; consistent because its completer targets q0:p0 = word [0,1,2,3,4,5] in hexagon 0, so its left-S6 canonicaliser fixes the hub hexagon

q1_event_history.anchor_state: immediately after that edge; completer.macro_index 74 == decoration.macro_index 74

part1_singleton.q1_key_observation: R1 itself merged R1 with the hub at macro-index 2 (hence MERGED_BY_R like the other 1182 F7 anchors); 72 edges later a Z3 first touched hexagon 0 and became the completer. The two events are independent -- the merge did not involve hexagon 0 at all.

q2_q3_r_joint_enumeration.candidates: 6 rotation lengths x 3 weight-3 moves = 18, computed against the real engine tables

rows.note: tq=0 IS in comp but source is not
tq=9 IS in comp but source is not

q2_q3_r_joint_enumeration.structure: perfectly anti-correlated -- whenever the source is in the component (rot 0, rot 3) every target is outside; whenever a target is in (rot 2, rot 5) the source is outside; no alignment

part1_singleton.q4_target_a_reachability: no one-step co-component R joint within the merged component; undecidable for other components (see part2 limits)

q5_known18.verdict: NOT APPLICABLE -- the question does not type-check
q5_known18.reason: this is a PRE-R2 frontier state (r_count=1); the three known-18 witnesses are POST-R2 boundary states -- different kinds of object
q5_known18.note: a non-match between a frontier state and a boundary state carries no information; no known-18 claim is made either way

q6_verdict.decisive_argument: its distinguishing feature is INVISIBLE to the Target-A predicate: target_a_recognizer reads r_count, joint_kind, state.F, state.H, after.hub_touch_count and incidence_components, and NEVER reads completer, event_order_class or branch (chaining is computed and explicitly not an acceptance condition)

orbit_changing_lemma.statement: every move in this engine maps a permutation into a DIFFERENT E-orbit
orbit_changing_lemma.consequence: for every R joint sq != tq necessarily, so Target-A same_component can never be satisfied trivially by source and target sharing one orbit; it always demands two DISTINCT orbits genuinely co-component

one_step_screen.candidates: 1818 anchors x 6 rotation lengths x 3 weight-3 moves = 32724
one_step_screen.per_family: 0 / n anchors possess a co-component one-step R joint, for all 24 families, no exception

theorem.name: one-step R1-component obstruction
theorem.statement: at every one of the 1818 residual anchors, no immediately-firing R joint -- at any of the 6 rotation lengths, with any of the 3 weight-3 moves -- has both its literal joint-source orbit and its target orbit inside the R1/hub merged component. Exhaustive over 32724 candidates, zero exceptions.

what_is_definitively_decided.detail: the 323 (False,True) and 51 (True,False) candidates cannot yield Target A -- if exactly one of sq,tq is in the merged component they are in different components, so same_component is false

what_is_NOT_decided.detail: both orbits lie outside the R1/hub component and could still be co-component in some THIRD component; the corpus carries only the R1 and hub components while O runs as high as 40 open orbits

limits_all_load_bearing: ONE STEP ONLY -- the immediate R joint from the anchor; says nothing about descendants whose p differs and whose components have grown monotonically
R1 COMPONENT ONLY -- a Target A lying wholly inside another component is untouched by this screen
COMPONENT RELATION ONLY -- legality is untested: target-window freshness, non-abandonment and om[tq]!=0 are all unchecked
part2_cocomponent.remaining_question: can any descendant of a residual anchor reach a state where the R2 joint source orbit and target orbit are co-component -- in the merged component or any other?
part2_cocomponent.data_request_that_would_make_this_decisi: the FULL component partition per anchor, not just the R1 and hub components
